items.slide_topic: work: voice demo (shown during the video Turing test discussion) - the 44-second Eleven v4 'what an AI voice can't do' spec ad
items.headline: Eleven v4 is INSANE!
items.dek: Here's my 44-sec spec ad for it. I wrote a script of everything an AI voice "can't do." Then made Eleven v4 read it out loud. Sound on
items.author: Burak Tuyan
items.caption: 44.05 s, 1920x1080 30 fps H.264 High + AAC-LC 44.1 kHz stereo, 19.6 MB, with audio. A stylised Louis-XIV-like caricature in a Versailles-style palace asks 'AI voices? Tell me something. Can they scream like THIS? And then fall apart like this? And sing when the moment demands... Fine, some of them whisper. But can they flirt in a whisper? Can they talk while eating? Or do an Italian accent? [Italian] Impossibile!' then 'Wait... Am I?' and an Eleven V4 / ElevenLabs end card. Burned-in subtitles; the X post carries a 'Made with AI' label.

transcript.burned_in_subtitle: And then fall apart like this?

transcript.speech_asr: And sing when the moment demands...
transcript.burned_in_subtitle: ♪ And sing when the moment demands ♪

transcript.burned_in_subtitle: But can they flirt in a whisper?

transcript.note: spoken tagline over the end card. Not subtitled. ASR (faster-whisper small.en) heard it as '11v4'; LinkedIn's auto-transcript of the same post renders it 'Eleven V4 the next frontier of human level communication?'. Treat the wording as machine-transcribed, not verbatim from a script.

items.origin: Downloaded with yt-dlp from the X post (HLS 1080p variant, 3.42 Mbps video + 128 kbps AAC); the direct twimg 1080p mp4 listed by fxtwitter has the same resolution, bitrate (3.42 Mbps) and size (19.57 MB), so this is the best quality X serves. Container remuxed with -c copy -movflags +faststart (no re-encode, no generation loss).
items.notes: Already H.264 High/yuv420p + AAC-LC and under 45 MB, so it was stream-copied rather than re-encoded (a re-encode could only lose quality). WHAT IT IS: a scripted, pre-rendered text-to-speech showcase (a fan-made 'spec ad'), NOT a real-time conversation, NOT a cloning demo and NOT an official product launch. Author's own bio says 'ex-ElevenLabs'; his self-reply says: 'This is a personal spec project. Not affiliated with or commissioned by ElevenLabs. Just a fan of what v4 can do, showing off something I've been waiting a long time for.' Voice = Eleven v4 per the author (post does not say whether standard v4 or v4 Turbo, nor which preset/cloned voice, nor which tags/prompts were used). Visuals appear to be AI-generated video (post labelled 'Made with AI'); the video model/tool is NOT named anywhere we could find. HOW NATURAL IT SOUNDS: I cannot listen to audio. What can be said from analysis: (1) speech-to-text recognised every scripted line cleanly, including the shouted line, the whispered lines and the Italian-accented word; (2) it contains non-verbal vocalisations (opening laugh, scream, a collapse/sob-like 'fall apart' line, a sung line) - the exact behaviours the script says AI voices 'can't do'; (3) delivery dynamic range is wide: RMS -18.2 dBFS (scream, peak -3.4) vs -28.8/-30.0 dBFS (whispers). Subjective realism is the author's claim ('INSANE') plus ~1.9M views; there is no blind test of this clip. For the talk: play it live with sound, then let the audience judge.

items.slide_topic: work: voice demo - latency claim (vendor chart)
items.headline: Median time to first speech
items.dek: Median time from request to audible speech. Measured September 2026 with identical scripts and default settings against Cartesia Sonic 3.6, xAI TTS, Google Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS, and OpenAI GPT-4o mini TTS. Eleven v4 Turbo over WebSocket streaming.
items.caption: Bar chart: Eleven v4 Turbo 150 ms; Cartesia Sonic 3.6 262 ms; xAI TTS 362 ms; Google Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS 685 ms; OpenAI GPT-4o mini TTS 814 ms
items.notes: VENDOR-REPORTED and vendor-run benchmark (footnote 3: network latency measured and removed for all systems). Light-background chart. Alt text on the page: 'Median time to first speech: Eleven v4 Turbo 150ms, fastest; others 262–814ms.' Downloaded from https://eleven-public-cdn.elevenlabs.io/payloadcms/1d5ten23khi-Latency-with-silence--2-.webp and converted to PNG.

items.slide_topic: work: voice demo - blind preference claim (vendor chart)
items.headline: Share of blind head-to-head pairs won by Eleven v4
items.dek: Based on blind head-to-head user preference testing against Cartesia Sonic 3.6, Inworld TTS-2, Google Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS, and Google Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, September 2026. For each pair, graders heard the same line from Eleven v4 and one competitor, presented blind, and judged which was more expressive; ties counted as half.
items.caption: Bar chart: v4 wins 81% vs Cartesia Sonic 3.6, 81% vs Inworld TTS-2, 72% vs Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS, 65% vs Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS
items.notes: VENDOR-REPORTED. Compares v4 against OTHER TTS MODELS, not against real humans - do not present it as a human-vs-AI Turing result. The chart text says 'more expressive'; the blog footnote 2 says graders judged both 'more expressive and which sounded more natural'. Source image https://eleven-public-cdn.elevenlabs.io/payloadcms/9hcvihiw58b-Expressiveness-chart--1-.webp

facts.claim: Burak Tuyan (bio: 'I tell stories. Sometimes for brands. | ex-ElevenLabs') posted a 44-second spec ad on Oct 2, 2026: 'I wrote a script of everything an AI voice "can't do." Then made Eleven v4 read it out loud.' It reached 1.9M views, 10,035 likes, 632 reposts, 444 replies, 6,211 bookmarks and 205 quotes within ~2 days.

The author's own disclosure: 'This is a personal spec project. Not affiliated with or commissioned by ElevenLabs. Just a fan of what v4 can do, showing off something I've been waiting a long time for.' (reply tweet; 265 likes, ~43.7K views)

The clip's script has the voice laugh, scream ('Can they scream like THIS?'), 'fall apart', sing ('And sing when the moment demands'), whisper ('Fine, some of them whisper. But can they flirt in a whisper?'), talk while eating, do an Italian accent ('Impossibile!'), then turn on itself: 'Wait... Am I?'
facts.source: Burned-in subtitles + speech-to-text of the video (our analysis)

facts.claim: ElevenLabs launched Eleven v4 and Eleven v4 Turbo on September 28, 2026: 'our most emotive text-to-speech model yet' plus a low-latency variant; available in ElevenAgents, ElevenCreative and the API.
facts.source: ElevenLabs launch post (Mati Staniszewski, Piotr Dabkowski); TechCrunch, Ivan Mehta

facts.claim: ElevenLabs claims Eleven v4 is 'Ranked #1 by Artificial Analysis' and 'preferred by ~75% of listeners in blind head-to-head tests over competing models' (vendor-run: wins 81%, 81%, 72%, 65% vs four rivals).
Artificial Analysis's Provider Voice Arena lists Eleven v4 first at Elo ~1321 (next: Qwen-Audio-3.1-TTS-Plus 1292, Cartesia Sonic 3.6 1278, Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS 1275); Eleven v3 sits at 1174.
facts.source: Artificial Analysis (independent, crowd-voted arena), page read 2026-10-04

facts.claim: Eleven v4 Turbo: ~100 ms median inference latency and ~150 ms median time to first speech (ElevenLabs-measured; rivals 262-814 ms) - 'it can respond faster than the average pause between two people talking.'
Eleven v4 supports 90+ languages, and Instant Voice Clones 'can now capture voices with high fidelity using just 10 seconds of audio'; a voice recorded in one language speaks any other fluently.
facts.source: ElevenLabs launch post; TechCrunch subhead 'ElevenLabs v4 can clone voices with a 10 second clip'

facts.claim: v4 is controlled with inline tags like [laughs], [said angrily in French accent], [light rain], [phone buzzing]; the company says it 'interprets tone, pacing, emotion, character, and context'.

Independent Turing-style evidence for voices: in a QMUL/UCL PLOS One study, 58% of AI voices cloned from real people were judged human vs 62% of real human voices judged human (no statistical difference); clones used off-the-shelf ElevenLabs software and under five minutes of speech (2025, older model).
facts.source: Live Science (2025-10-04); The Register, 'Humans flunk the Turing test for voices as bots get chattier' (2025-10-09)

facts.claim: A July 2026 blind study of 1,326 weekly radio listeners found AI and human voiceover scored nearly identically; reactions diverged once listeners learned the source.
facts.source: Radio Ink (study by Harker Bos Group)

facts.claim: Voice-clone risk is already a political issue: on April 16, 2026 Sen. Maggie Hassan pressed ElevenLabs, LOVO, Speechify and VEED to prevent scammers abusing voice cloning, as the FBI reported $893 million in AI-related scam losses in 2025.
facts.source: U.S. Joint Economic Committee press release; CNN Business (2026-05-29)

facts.claim: Framing caveat for the slide: the demo is scripted, pre-rendered text-to-speech by a (former-ElevenLabs) fan - not real-time conversation, not a cloning demo and not an official launch video; there is no blind test of this clip.
facts.source: Our reading of the post, the author's disclosure and the launch materials
